This page lets you rebuild the structure of `src/scgsim` from one place: which
stages exist, the order the work flows through them on the Palace route and on
the AEDT route, what crosses from one stage to the next, and which folder is
which stage. A *stage* is a folder that takes what an earlier stage produced
and produces what a later stage reads. The tables on this page are generated
from the folders' own docstrings, so they say what the code says.

## The two routes {#routes}

Both routes start from a layout and a stack and end at a result a person reads;
they are the two routes of the [backend support matrix](backend-support.qmd).
Every square box is a folder below `src/scgsim`, named as the folder is; a
rounded box is outside SCGSim. A solid
arrow is an import: the stage at its head imports the stage at its tail, or,
where the arrow says *calls*, the stage at its tail calls the one at its head.
A dashed arrow is a file or a value handed over, labelled with what it is and,
where a contract module defines the file, with that module.

```{mermaid}
%%| column: screen-inset
flowchart TB
  layout(["layout and stack"]) -. "components or GDS, stack" .-> gsource
  subgraph shared["shared geometry"]
    gsource["geometry/source"] --> ginterp["geometry/interpretation"]
    ginterp -- "calls as its last step" --> gjunc["geometry/junctions"]
  end
  ginterp --> psource
  ginterp --> gplan
  subgraph palace_route["Palace route"]
    subgraph simulation["palace/simulation calls"]
      psource["palace/source"] --> pmesh["palace/mesh"]
      pmesh -- "calls" --> gsepr["geometry/surface_epr"]
      gsepr -- "calls" --> gsgb["geometry/sgb"]
      gsgb -. "XAO and sidecar<br/>contracts/sgb_sidecar" .-> meshing["meshing"]
      pmesh -- "calls" --> meshing
      pmesh --> pconfig["palace/config"]
      pconfig -. "config.json<br/>contracts/palace_run_folder" .-> prun["palace/run"]
    end
    prun -. "run folder" .-> palace_solver(["Palace"])
    palace_solver -. "returned run folder<br/>contracts/palace_run_folder" .-> presults["palace/results"]
    presults --> preports["palace/reports"]
  end
  subgraph aedt_route["AEDT route"]
    gplan["geometry/planning"] --> aprep
    aspecs["aedt/specs"] --> aprep["aedt/preparation"]
    aprep -. "handoff folder" .-> aruntime["aedt/runtime"]
    aruntime -- "calls" --> aepr["aedt/epr"]
    gplan --> aepr
    aruntime -. "run folder and receipt" .-> aresults["aedt/results"]
    aepr --> aresults
    aresults -- "calls" --> apres["aedt/presentation"]
  end
```

The diagram leaves out the folders every stage of an area uses:
`geometry/models` and `geometry/grid` in geometry, `geometry/sgb/exact` in SGB,
and `semantics` and `presentation` across the package. AEDT's handoff and
receipt formats are defined in `aedt/specs` and `aedt/results`, not in
`contracts`. `visualization` reads a Palace run folder or an AEDT project to
draw a geometry preview; it is not a step of either route. The stage tables
below list every folder.

## How to read a folder {#read-a-folder}

Every package folder's `__init__.py` opens with one sentence that says what the
folder is. A stage folder adds three lines:

```text
<one sentence: what the folder is>

In: what the stage takes, and from which stage
Out: what the stage produces
Next: which stage reads that
```

Imports point against the flow: a later stage imports an earlier one, and an
earlier stage does not import a later one. A stage that drives others is the
one exception by design: `palace/simulation` imports each Palace stage it runs,
`geometry/interpretation` calls `geometry/junctions` as its last step, and
`aedt/runtime` calls the in-AEDT part of `aedt/epr`. These imports also point
from an earlier stage to a later one:

| Importing folder | Imports | What it takes from there |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `geometry/junctions` | `geometry/sgb` | SGB's boundary binder (`prisms.bound_rings`) and exact records, so the partition cuts the rings SGB builds. |
| `palace/results` | `palace/reports` | The report views a resolved result's display methods return. |
| `aedt/specs` | `aedt/epr` | The grouping of surface integrals (`epr.selection`). |
| `aedt/preparation` | `aedt/results` | The receipt schema and the initial receipt (`results.provenance`). |
| `aedt/results` | `aedt/runtime`, `aedt/epr`, `aedt/presentation` | The batch collection context and benchmark path, the `EprResult` record, and the display a `ResolvedRun` calls. |

## Stage tables {#stage-tables}

Each area has one table, its rows in the order the work flows through it. A
row's text is the folder's docstring: *What it is* is the first sentence, and
In, Out and Next are the three lines. A folder that is not a stage says in
its In cell what it is instead: an area's own folder, a part of the stage in
the row it names, or a stage whose docstring names its modules.

To change a row, edit the folder's docstring and run
`python scripts/generate_code_map.py`; the order of the rows is stated once, in
that script. The script refuses a package folder it does not list and a stage
whose docstring lacks one of the three lines, and
`tests/test_code_map.py` fails while the tables differ from the docstrings.

{{< include _code-map-stages.md >}}

## Where to put new code {#new-code}

- A helper lives in the earliest stage that calls it, and later stages import
  it from there.
- What only AEDT's native construction calls lives in `geometry/planning`;
  nothing on the Palace route imports that folder.
- `geometry/models` imports no other geometry code, and `contracts` imports
  nothing else from `scgsim` and no third-party package, so every stage can
  import them. The import-linter contract `contracts-import-nothing-else`
  checks `contracts`.
- A new package folder goes into `AREAS` in `scripts/generate_code_map.py`
  where the work reaches it, with the sentence and, for a stage, the three
  lines in its `__init__.py`.
